title: In the north you're booking light
subtitle: Not weather. The hours of usable daylight are the thing you are actually paying for.

text: Above the Arctic Circle at midsummer, the sun does not set.
sub: Which changes the shape of the whole day. Dinner at nine still reads as afternoon, and the fjords hold a level glow for hours.

title: What each window actually gives you

points.label: Late May
points.value: Meltwater in the falls, long days, and a season still finding its feet ashore.

points.label: June
points.value: The midnight-sun weeks. The most light you will ever be sold, and the reason to go.

points.label: July
points.value: Still bright, warmer ashore, and the busiest weeks of the northern deployment.

points.label: August
points.value: Darkness returning at the edges. Quieter towns, and the first aurora nights late on.

points.label: September
points.value: The season closing. Colour ashore, real night skies, and less margin in the weather.

title: Three honest trades in the north

items.head: Midnight sun or night sky
items.body: You cannot have both on one voyage. Aurora needs darkness, and midsummer has none to offer.

items.head: Waterfalls or warmth ashore
items.body: Early season runs full and cold. High summer is kinder to sit outside in and quieter on the falls.

items.head: Long days or empty towns
items.body: The weeks with the most light are the weeks with the most company. Pick which one you came for.

text: Name the hours you want, and the month names itself.
sub: This is the whole northern conversation. Not which ship, not which fjord — how much light you want to be awake in, and what you'll trade for it.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Then tell me whether you're chasing the midnight sun or the first dark nights, and I'll draft the fortnight around it.
